newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees '97 peso averaging 8.4-8.5 - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees '97 peso averaging 8.4-8.5 - newspaper.

text.p: The Mexican government estimates the peso will average an exchange rate of between 8.40 and 8.50 pesos per dollar in 1997, the daily newspaper Reforma reported in Thursday editions.

Citing advances of Mexico's budget proposals for 1997, which later Thursday will be made public when sent to Congress, Reforma said the peso estimates were based on inflation differences between the United States and Mexico.
"It is an estimate and should not be considered an objective of the government," one unnamed government official was quoted as saying.

Reforma said other budget details to be announced included an expected five percent rise in tax collections, a nine percent increase in social spending and a five percent cut in public spending that is not linked to social welfare.

Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz will explain today that the aim of the budget policy for next year is to contribute to financial stability and at the same time consolidate a recovery of growth, Reforma said.
Reforma said there would be big cuts in non-priority spending in 1997 given the government's aim to support banks and pension funds.

"Given that the government will have to spend 0.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) on the support program for banks and 0.63 percent on the payment of social pensions in the second half of 1997, there will be big cuts in non-priority expenses to keep the (public sector) deficit at only 0.5 percent of GDP at the end of the year," Reforma said.
Expectations are for a deficit in Mexico's current account of between $4 billion to $5 billion, it added.
Estimates are for a 2 percent increase in direct public investment but a 20 percent jump in investment driven by the public sector, Reforma said.
